findings.title: Corrections target 361 artifacts that do not exist, and silently re-own the shared contract
findings.description:
Both "corrections" are written as retrofit fixes to text in `commands/analysis/understand.md` and to "the generated `943` sample". I verified neither exists: `commands/analysis/` contains only `tech-debt-audit.md`, `project-documents/user/analysis/` contains only `940`/`941`/`942`, and 361 is `status: not_started` (its own task file has graph generation as the still-open Task 0.1). Grepping the 361 **design** also finds no claim that `layers[].nodeIds` mixes function/class nodes and no intersect-with-`type=="file"` instruction — the only related text is `select(.type == "file" or ...)`. So the slice is correcting a skill text that 361's implementer has not yet authored, and it is not pinned to anything in the 361 design.

Two consequences the design does not handle. First, the slice plan makes 361 the sole owner of "the graph-reading contract — validation, staleness, extraction, provenance", and 362's own Integration Points section says 364 consumes "the corrected layer composition and the file-level definition". Redefining "file-level" and the layer-count rule from 362 means the shared contract now has two owners, and 363/364's designs will read whichever document they were pointed at. Second, the framing ("not merely additive", "a defect fix inside squadron, not an escalation") is doing load-bearing work in the scope statement and will be re-litigated at implementation when the implementer finds nothing to correct.

Fix: state these as **amendments to the 361 contract** and land them in the 361 design (or a named handoff, as 361's tasks already do for F011/F012), so one authoritative definition of "file-level" exists before 363/364 design against it. Keep the mapping table in 362 and let it reference that definition.

findings.title: "Verified graph facts" and the acceptance criteria bind to measurements of a graph this repo does not have
findings.description:
The table is presented as "measurements, not assumptions, and the design's decisions rest on them" (v2.8.1, `gitCommitHash` `1bfbca1`, 925 nodes / 238 analyzed files / 27 `entry-point` tags). `.understand-anything/` does not exist in this repo — a fact 361's own task file records as a blocking anchor ("`.understand-anything/` **does not exist in this repo** — Task 0.1 is a hard prerequisite for every walkthrough task", and generating it is PM-gated). 362's walkthrough step 1 asks the implementer to re-run those `jq` probes and step 2 predicts index **944** because "943 exists"; success criteria 4 and 5 make the literal counts (`34`, `6`, `238`) pass/fail conditions. As written, the first implementation action is either a dead run (no graph) or a hard stop for a non-defect reason: any graph regeneration after new commits changes `analyzedFiles`, and step 1's instruction is to **stop** when the numbers disagree.

Fix (two parts, both cheap): (a) add the missing prerequisite line to the walkthrough — the graph exists only after 361 Task 0.1, and its absence is that prerequisite failing, not drift; (b) restate SC4/SC5 as the *invariants* the design actually depends on (`Σ layers[].nodeIds == meta.analyzedFiles == count of non-function/class nodes`, and "a layer containing non-`file` types reports its breakdown"), with `34`/`6`/`238` demoted to "observed at design time on `1bfbca1`". The invariant version is what makes the coverage section verifiable on any repo — which is the stated goal, since the capability's purpose is analyzing *other* people's codebases.

findings.title: Section-closing observations are neither mapped to fields nor marked, against the traceability rule the same section asserts
findings.description:
The design commits to two rules — the mapping table is "binding" per section, and "a section is never filled with prose that is not traceable to its named fields" (echoed by success criterion 3, "every claim traces to node, edge, layer, tour, or metadata") — then carves out "the closing observation each section carries — the sentence that reads a pattern out of the data". That content type appears nowhere in the seven-row mapping table, has no source-field list, and is explicitly barred from the only marker the flow has (`[INFERRED]` is banned here). The offered test — "if the sentence is not derivable from the table directly above it, it does not belong" — is a reader's judgment, not the "mechanical" test it claims to be.

The requirement this leaves unmet is the architecture's: the provenance block records "which sections came from source data", so a provenance line will assert field-sourcing for a section that ends in an unlabeled machine interpretation — precisely the "human trusting a partly-invented document" failure the provenance block exists to guard, and adjacent to the "never fabricate intent" design goal. Fix by either naming the observation in the mapping table (source = the section's own presented rows, form = restatement of a count/ranking already shown, no new noun), or giving it a distinct marker, or dropping it — one of the three, stated.

findings.title: "Reused verbatim by 363" overstates: the mapping has no row sourcing `config` nodes, which the architecture's Initial Technical Direction row requires
findings.description:
The Value section claims the extraction mapping "is reused verbatim by slice 363", and Provides-to-363 names project identity → Initial Technical Direction, layers/tour → Solution Approach. The parent architecture's interview-scope table specifies Initial Technical Direction ← `project.languages`, `project.frameworks`, **and `config` nodes**. None of the seven mapping rows sources `config`-type nodes as content; they surface only inside aggregate counts (17 `config` nodes in the type-breakdown facts, 13 inside one layer's count). Section 7's "config" row is `config.json`, the upstream settings file — a different thing with a confusable name. So 363's extract-then-ask for ITD lands on a mapping that yields languages/frameworks and no config-node evidence, and either re-derives it (duplicating 362's read logic, which the plan's "implemented once" rationale forbids) or asks a question the graph can answer.

Fix: add a `config`-node line to section 1 (stack evidence alongside `languages`/`frameworks` — the nodes are already inside the 238-node selection, so the marginal cost is one grouping), or state explicitly that `config` nodes are 363's own selection and drop the "verbatim" claim. Also disambiguate "`config` nodes" vs "`config.json`" in the text.

findings.title: New drift cross-checks are unstated about where they run, and unenumerated for their third cases
findings.description:
The slice declares the 361 preflight "executed unchanged" and puts any change to "the preflight contract's validation/staleness/hygiene behavior" in the Excluded list, yet introduces three validation-shaped checks: every `nodeIds` entry must resolve to a node carrying `filePath`; a node surviving the type filter without `filePath` "is reported as drift"; and section 6 resolves edge endpoints to their owning file's layer. It is not stated which of these preflight owns and which the extraction flow owns — an implementer extending `understand.md` cannot tell whether adding the `nodeIds` check means editing the "unchanged" contract section. And the enumeration is incomplete for the cases the walk-through's own `jq` already invents: the step-1 probe writes `//"UNRESOLVED"` for a `nodeIds` entry whose id is absent from `nodes[]`, which is neither a function/class hit nor a clean pass, and is unhandled by the prose. Likewise, section 6's endpoint→layer resolution has no stated outcome for an owning file that is absent from `nodes[]` or belongs to no layer, and no case for an intra-file self-edge across the excluded types.

Fix: add a short placement line per check (preflight vs flow) and one row each for unresolved-id / unlayered-endpoint, with the same "report as drift, never silently filter" strategy the design already chose for the resolved-but-wrong-type case. The design's own no-silent-filter principle is the right handling; it just needs to be extended to these two paths.

findings.title: Two 900-band facts in the design are stale but harmless to the decision
findings.description: Walkthrough step 2's "943 exists, so expect 944" and the implementation note about the 943 sample both presuppose 361's run having happened. Since index selection is defined as "lowest unused ≥ 940" and re-runs are independent samples (architecture-sanctioned overflow past 949), nothing here needs new architecture — but the specific predicted index will be wrong whenever the numbering shifts, and criteria that name a concrete file are the ones that age. Worth phrasing as "the next unused index, which is not any existing file's" at implementation time.
